what: BorgWarner makes drivetrain and propulsion parts: turbochargers, timing systems and transmission components for combustion engines, and motors, inverters and battery systems for electric vehicles.
customers: Carmakers worldwide, who design its components into vehicle platforms years before production.
money: timing chains, clutches and all-wheel-drive systems
electric motors, inverters and battery packs
moat: Components designed into a vehicle platform stay there for the model's life, typically five to seven years, which makes the revenue visible far ahead.
risks: A 1.9% net margin and earnings that depend on global vehicle production volumes
The electric vehicle transition has slowed, and the electric segment is not yet profitable
$4.1B of debt, though against $2.3B of cash
opportunities: 8.4 times free cash flow with $1.2B of free cash flow against a $9.9B market value
Analysts see about 58% upside, with 15 covering the stock
Turbochargers are needed on hybrids too, so a slower electric transition helps the profitable half
watch: Growth relative to global vehicle production, and the electric segment's losses.
